goal: Design an arterial-channel that reproduces mid-range arterial wall shear, 15 dyn/cm^2 (1.5 Pa), and pick the geometry and flow that achieve it.
source: Arterial wall shear stress ~10-20 dyn/cm^2 (1-2 Pa); target 1.5 Pa (mid-range). Papaioannou & Stefanadis, Hellenic J Cardiol 2005;46(1):9-15, PMID 15807389.

goal: Measure barrier integrity of a Caco-2 monolayer on a 1.12 cm² 12-well Transwell insert. The cell-free blank reads 150 Ω; the seeded insert reads 900 Ω. With 50 µM of a paracellular probe in the donor and a steady-state flux of 0.03 nmol/min, report the TEER (Ω·cm²), the apparent permeability Papp (cm/s) and the clearance (mL/min).
source: TEER = (R_total − R_blank) × A and Papp = (flux/60)/(A·C0): standard Transwell QC (Millipore/Costar app notes). Caco-2 TEER 250–1000 Ω·cm²; hCMEC/D3 (BBB) higher — Gericke et al., Fluids Barriers CNS 2020, doi:10.1186/s12987-020-00212-5.

goal: A suspension of primary human hepatocytes is counted on a hemocytometer: a mean of 40 cells per 1 mm^2 corner square at a 1:2 dilution. From 0.36 mL of this suspension, how many wells of a 96-well plate can be plated at the standard sandwich-culture plating density?
source: Blind design target: primary human hepatocyte sandwich-culture plating density 1.5e5 cells/cm^2 — Bioengineering 2023;10(2):131, doi:10.3390/bioengineering10020131 (goal text does NOT state the density). Hemocytometer formula (mean cells/square × dilution × 1e4) — CSH Protocols 2008, doi:10.1101/pdb.prot4498. conc = 40 × 2 × 1e4 = 8e5; total = 8e5 × 0.36 = 2.88e5; per well = 1.5e5 × 0.32 (96-well) = 48000; wells = 2.88e5 / 48000 = 6.

goal: Culture human proximal tubular epithelial cells in a microchannel that reproduces the apical fluid shear these cells experience in vivo — approximately 0.2 dyn/cm². Choose geometry and flow accordingly, and report the wall shear stress in Pa.
source: Blind design target (unit-ambiguity): the canonical kidney PTEC apical FSS is 0.2 dyn/cm^2 = 0.02 Pa (Jang et al., Integrative Biology 2013, 10.1039/c3ib40049b). The goal states the target in dyn/cm^2; the model must convert (×0.1) to Pa — a dyn/cm^2-as-Pa misread gives 0.2 Pa, a 10× error. blind_strength is None: the magnitude is given, so this tests unit conversion, not cold recall.

goal: A lab sets up 3D culture in 96-well ultra-low-attachment plates, one spheroid per well. What is the standard working medium volume per well?
source: 96-ULA working volume 100 uL/well — Corning spheroid-microplate protocol (CLS-AN-235), Sartorius/IncuCyte, PerkinElmer ATPlite 3D. Stated in the Labwright system prompt (96-ULA = 100 uL/well), so prompt-backed.

goal: Design a venular channel recapitulating physiological venular wall shear stress. Choose geometry and flow that achieve the physiological target.
source: Blind design target: mid-range venular WSS 3 dyn/cm^2 = 0.3 Pa (venular range ~1-6 dyn/cm^2). Papaioannou & Stefanadis 2005, PMID 15807389; Koutsiaris et al., Biorheology 2007;44(5-6):375-386, PMID 18401076. The goal text does NOT state the number.

goal: A body-on-chip skin compartment is scaled to an adult (70 kg, cardiac output 5000 mL/min) and the chip carries 5e6 cells. Report the skin compartment's organ flow fraction and the organ flow rate (mL/min) it receives.
source: Blind design target (cold): skin flow is ~6% of cardiac output in the committed body-on-chip flow-fraction table (labwright/calc/scaling.py:ORGAN_FLOW_FRACTIONS, sourced to Ucciferri et al. 2014, doi:10.3389/fbioe.2014.00074). Honest note: skin flow conventions range ~6–10% of cardiac output; the committed project table pins 0.06 and the gold targets the project standard. The goal text states neither the fraction nor the flow; not in the Labwright system prompt either.

goal: A recirculating liver-on-chip has a total system volume (reservoir + chip + tubing) of 200 uL and is dosed at an inlet of 10 uM; the outlet reads 7 uM at a perfusion flow of 2 uL/min. What is the elimination half-life in hours (t1/2 = ln2 x V / Cl, Cl = E x Q)?
source: self-consistent (formula): Cl = (1 - 7/10) x 2 = 0.6 uL/min; t1/2 = ln2 x 200 / 0.6 = 231.0 min = 3.851 h (min -> h via /60, handled by the calculator). Rowland & Tozer, single-compartment half-life.

goal: A repeat-dose study doses a chip with a compound whose half-life is 12 h, every 24 h. Report the steady-state accumulation ratio.
source: self-consistent (formula): R = 1/(1 - exp(-ln2 x 24 / 12)) = 1/(1 - 0.25) = 1.33 (interval = 2 x t1/2). Gibaldi & Perrier (accumulation factor).

goal: Venous endothelium on-chip at 1.0 Hz in a 150 µm channel (water: 0.001 Pa·s, 1000 kg/m³), mean shear 0.10 Pa with amplitude 0.08 Pa, flow 8/2/5 µL/min (peak/min/mean). Give Womersley number, OSI, peak shear (Pa) and PI.
source: Womersley α = r√(ωρ/μ) (Womersley 1955); OSI (Ku et al. 1985); PI (Gosling & King 1974). Heart-on-chip aortic inflow: mean shear 0.59 Pa at 1.2 Hz, α=0.27, OSI=0.2 — Wang et al., microfluidic flow-profile generator (Lab Chip).
